overview: This bill, the Returning SBA to Main Street Act of 2025, would require the Small Business Administration (SBA), the federal agency that helps small businesses with loans and counseling, to move at least 30 percent of its headquarters employees out of the Washington, D.C., area to its regional offices around the country, if the agency's head determines this would save the government money. Moved employees would be paid at the local rate for their new location and could not telework full time, and other full-time teleworkers who stay tied to headquarters would also lose full-time telework. Employees who telework as a disability accommodation would be exempt. The SBA would also have to cut its headquarters office space by at least 30 percent within two years and report staffing and telework numbers to Congress each year, and the bill would override union contracts. As of May 21, 2025, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say moving staff closer to the small businesses they serve would improve in-person help across the country while cutting office costs in Washington.
against: Critics say forced relocations and the end of full-time telework could push experienced employees to quit, disrupt the agency's work, and override agreements reached with employee unions.
